A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work, with matching authors, research questions and core analysis. All 36 pages of v1 and 49 pages of v2, including figures, equations, tables and appendices, are readable and support comparison.

before.justification: Sections 4.1–4.2 and Appendix D report original synthetic regression and UTKFace experiments, including sample-size scaling, teacher comparisons and label-noise tests.

after.justification: The original regression experiments remain, and Appendices E.2–E.3 add original ColoredMNIST and SST-2 classification results.

M1.justification: The two-stage W2S workflow remains. Added classification applications use cross-entropy probing and confidence-weighted W2S loss for full SST-2 finetuning. Equations (2)–(5) also replace summed squared losses with sample averages. Ridge regression itself was already specified and used in v1.

E1.justification: v2 adds pooled-color ColoredMNIST binary digit classification and SST-2 movie-review sentiment classification. These substantially extend coverage beyond synthetic regression and UTKFace age estimation, which are retained.

E2.justification: The comparison methods remain the weak teacher, strong supervised baseline and strong ceiling model. Existing experiments retain their comparator membership. The added studies introduce different backbone configurations while retaining these comparison roles, rather than evaluating a new competing W2S method.

E3.justification: New protocols include DINOv2/ResNet classification probing for 800 steps, Electra/BERT full finetuning for three epochs, SST-2 evaluation with 0-1 loss, and SAID-based intrinsic-dimension estimation. Equations (2)–(5) also change loss normalization while the stated UTKFace regularization remains 10^-6, revising the written finite-regularization specification without establishing that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: Figures 10–13 add teacher-discrepancy and label-flipping analyses on both classification tasks. ColoredMNIST explicitly selects teachers with similar intrinsic dimensions but different correlation dimensions, strengthening the control of that comparison. These extend the original regression-based investigations of discrepancy and noise.

E5.justification: Both versions specify standard deviations over 40 synthetic runs and 10 UTKFace runs. v2 does not revise these counts or introduce significance tests or confidence intervals. Additional classification plots have error bars, but their run counts and uncertainty definitions are not specified.

E6.justification: Figures 10–13 and Tables 2–3 add classification outcomes and dimension measurements. Existing Figure 2 also changes: at displayed n=2000, N=4000 and correlation dimension 90, W2S excess risk shifts from approximately 7e-4 to 4e-4, reversing its ordering against S-Baseline at approximately 6e-4. The accompanying failure-to-outperform statement remains unchanged. Table 1's dimension changes are only finer rounding.

T1.justification: New Appendix C adds Assumption 3, revised capacity and alignment quantities, and Theorem 3 with a ridge-regression variance/bias derivation and optimized regularization bounds. This substantially expands v1's informal ridge discussion. Appendix B.1 also restores a missing V_w V_w^T factor in an inverse-covariance expectation; the canonical-angle appendix is retained under renumbering.

C1.justification: The three stated contributions and central claims about discrepancy-driven variance reduction, intrinsic dimension and PGR/OPR scaling remain. The abstract's added mention of NLP updates the supporting empirical coverage without redefining those core claims.

C2.justification: Section 4.2 replaces its stratified comparison against the smaller intrinsic dimension with an interpretation based on correlation dimension divided by weak intrinsic dimension. Appendix C newly explains how regularization and larger sample sizes can compensate for alignment-related error. Section 5's limitations remain unchanged.

D1.justification: v2 adds optimizer, learning-rate, weight-decay, warmup and training-budget details, plus SAID's 90% accuracy threshold and gradient subsampling, randomized rangefinding and QR instructions. These substantially expand reproducibility documentation, although the SST-2 sample description and the stated sketch-matrix dimensions contain internal inconsistencies.

R1.justification: Ten references are added for the new datasets, architectures, optimization and sketching, including Arjovsky et al., Clark et al., Oquab et al., Halko et al. and Woodruff et al. Section 1.1 and Appendix A retain their substantive positioning relative to earlier W2S and distillation research.

P1.justification: Most existing prose and the main section order remain. v2 makes targeted wording and notation clarifications, rewrites the experimental overview and correlation-dimension discussion, and adds an appendix contents list with an expanded appendix hierarchy. The scientific additions do not entail extensive rewriting of the retained narrative.

P2.justification: v2 restyles existing plots, changes Figure 5's legend normalization, and adds four multipanel figures and two dimension tables. Existing UTKFace Table 1 and Figures 7–9 are reflowed within Appendix E.1. This is a substantial expansion and revision of the visual presentation.

improvement.justification: The classification and full-finetuning experiments extend v1's regression-only validation, while the ColoredMNIST teacher selection better controls intrinsic dimension. However, revised Figure 2 contradicts its retained interpretation. The new ridge proof also loses a factor N in the expectation calculation on page 38, given the isotropic rows in Equation (17), leaving its claimed sample-size scaling unsupported by that derivation. These empirical gains and material reliability problems prevent a confident net-quality judgment.
